design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (installation_scheduling_and_job_charges, env_0060). Step 0 draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5, 4, 6, 4]; assigned: trim capping charge 6, customer reschedule fee 5, permit filing fee 4, crew-date booking 4 (multiset equal to the draw).

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Ruth Kowalski only asks to add aluminum trim capping to all thirteen windows of her opened Full-Frame Installation job. The capping rule prices the capping against a booked crew date ('The trim capping charge is fixed only once the job record carries a booked crew date.'), but she released her last date on 2026-10-06, so the job is opened with no date. Booking a crew date in turn waits on two record states that are false in her ledger: the permit administration fee of the permitted job ('For a permitted job, the crew days booked are fixed only after the job's charges carry the permit administration fee.') and the late reschedule fee for her 36-hour release ('A crew date for a job whose earlier crew date the customer moved or released is not booked until the job's charges carry the late reschedule fee owed for every such customer reschedule that was late or beyond the free count.'). The agent must read the three sentences, check the job, its activities and contracts, see that none of the states holds, and work out from the other rules which write brings each about. Each write is itself a multi-factor computation over the ledger and other products (contracts, change orders, factory order, door contract, CareLine plan). Difficulty comes from reading policy, querying the world and calculating, never from choosing among similar tools: each of the four tools is the only tool for its business action.

2. SCOPE. Task 0 is the first task: nothing was occupied. It claims install_ext_permit_filing_fee, install_ext_customer_reschedule_fee, install_ext_crew_date_booking, install_ext_trim_capping_charge and the tools assess_permit_admin_fee_bf2a1df3, assess_reschedule_fee_4c3399da, book_crew_date_2f98f590, approve_trim_capping_649df03e (user). Reserved for task 1 (draw: 3 prerequisites, factors [6,6,6,6]): the credit side of the job charges (late-arrival credit, company reschedule credit), the failed-access fee and a second customer-approved added-work charge (new interior casing on an Insert Pocket job), all on an in-progress job; no task-0 policy or tool is needed there.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root R = install_ext_trim_capping_charge (on_request, owner user). Edges: (a) R <- install_ext_crew_date_booking, value_input, gate lead_days, state form, sentence 'The trim capping charge is fixed only once the job record carries a booked crew date.', condition install_jobs.scheduled_date booked; false at frozen_time: install_jobs.<job>.status = opened, scheduled_date = '' (release row a_r3 has new_date ''). Only book_crew_date_2f98f590 writes scheduled_date among this difficulty's tools. (b) booking <- install_ext_permit_filing_fee, value_input, gate inspection_hold, state form, sentence quoted above; false: permit_required true, no permit_admin_fee row on the job. Only assess_permit_admin_fee_bf2a1df3 writes a permit_admin_fee row. (c) booking <- install_ext_customer_reschedule_fee, state_gate, gate install_activities.fee_kind, state form, negated direction ('is not booked until'), condition: every late or beyond-free customer reschedule carries a late_reschedule_fee dated its request date; false: a_r3 (2026-10-06, 36 h) has none, the only late fee a_fee1 is dated 2026-09-30. Only assess_reschedule_fee_4c3399da writes late_reschedule_fee rows. Value_input edges: 2 of 3 = max(3-1,1). Four-point test on each sentence: explicit connective (only once / only after / not ... until), a record-visible state on the waited side, no tool/policy id/code token, strength 'only/not until' as intended and scope limited to permitted jobs / customer-moved jobs. Directions: two affirmative, one negated - a booking 'is not booked until' its fees stand is how a scheduling desk phrases it, a charge 'is fixed only after/once' what it rests on is how billing phrases it. Topological order: permit fee, reschedule fee (parallel, commute), booking, capping. Deletion sensitivity (sens.py): skip permit fee -> crew days 5 instead of 6; skip booking -> capping computation raises (no date) and the job stays opened; skip reschedule fee -> crew days unchanged (state gate), terminal state lacks the 37.50 row. user_scenario mentions no permit, fee or booking duty; tools validate nothing.

4. FACTOR CARD (sens.py run at each handling time; figures are result with that factor at its baseline).
Permit filing fee (step 10, expected 89.40, all-baseline 95.00): window_schedule_basis (method) 13 openings on RW-26-318402 -> flat fee + 4.00 per opening beyond 12 = 99.00, baseline flat 95.00 -> 87.00; contract_valuation_band (parameter) price 15450.24 -> +30.00, baseline 0 -> 71.40; safety_glazing_count (parameter) 2 tempered openings by change order -> +20.00, baseline 0 -> 77.40; shared_filing_share (parameter, multi-source: contract status AND signing gap) ordered door contract RD-26-307215 signed the same day -> 0.6, baseline 1 -> 149.00. Near-miss: the closed 2021 door contract RD-21-304417 is not 'released to the factory and not yet installed' and is not a filing partner.
Customer reschedule fee (step 12, expected 37.50, all-baseline 175.00): contract_size_adder (parameter, cross window) 13 openings -> +25.00 -> 32.81; notice_proration (method) 36 h -> pro-rated 200.00 x 12/48 = 50.00, baseline whole base -> 150.00; ridgeline_move_share (parameter) one company move a_r2 -> 0.5 -> 75.00; repeat_late_factor (parameter) one standing late fee a_fee1 -> 1.25 -> 30.00; crew_date_release_factor (parameter) release with no new date -> 1.2 -> 31.25. Near-miss: the earlier 20-hour reschedule a_r1 would give the whole base; the rule prices the most recent customer reschedule.
Crew-date booking (step 14, expected 6, all-baseline 3): build_class_pace (parameter, cross order) FO-2026-31377 Custom Color Build -> pace -1 -> 4; series_frame_pace (parameter, cross window) 5500 Series Fiberglass -> pace -1 -> 4; inspection_hold_back (parameter, multi-source: permit fee on the job AND units) -> 1 opening -> 5; oversize_day_count (method, cross window) 3 oversize at the 2026-07-24 measure -> weighted 15.5 / 3 -> 6, baseline count -> 5. Near-miss: the door order FO-2026-31378 is a Custom Size Build (no cut) but belongs to the door contract, not this job's factory order.
Trim capping charge (step 16, expected 1342.59, all-baseline 1157.00): oversize_coil_weight (parameter) 3 oversize -> 1.5 each -> 1234.76; priced_opening_tiers (method) 14.5 priced openings -> 10 at 89.00 + 4.5 at 75 percent = 1190.375, baseline 89.00 x 14.5 -> 1423.70; color_matched_coil (parameter, multi-source: exterior color change order AND series) -> 22.00 per priced opening -> 1084.20; short_lead_coil_order (parameter, multi-source: lead days AND color order) 2026-10-19 is 6 days out -> 120.00 -> 1222.59; contract_program_carryover (parameter, cross window tier parameter) senior -> 0.04 (5500 senior_discount_pct) -> 1402.97; careline_parts_discount (parameter, cross service) CareLine Plus active -> 0.15 -> 1569.00. Near-miss: the door contract's single unit is not an opening of this job (13, not 14).
Inherited base boundaries: capping only where the method offers it and does not include it (Full-Frame: available, not included); permit fee only for a permitted job; reschedule fees only for late or beyond-free customer reschedules, failed-access visits keep the failed-access fee; crew days still rounded up to whole days. Overwrites (each names its own scope and keeps the in-force parts): install_reschedules late-fee sentence (amount only, failed-access and free-count parts restated); install_permits 'charges the method's permit administration fee once per job on the job's opened date' (amount only, once/opened date kept); install_scheduling crew-day sentence (method only, rounding kept); install_site_charges 'exterior trim capping is charged per opening only where the method offers it and does not include it' (round 2: only the per-opening capping clause is retired; its replaced_by keeps the 'only where the method offers it and does not include it' condition and the work-date dating, names its own scope 'for exterior trim capping that the customer approves, and only for such capping', and excludes new interior casing by name; the general sentence 'Conditions found or requested at the home are charged on the job, each at the method's rate, on the date the work is done.' stays in force for every condition).

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Fee writes (steps 10, 12, 16; subject install_fee_assessed): install_lead_safe.pre_1978_home satisfied (customers.home_year_built 1949, bound by customer_id), install_permits.permitted_job satisfied (install_jobs.permit_required true, bound by install_job_id), install_agg_concurrent_jobs / install_reschedules / install_site_charges policy scope (each charge on the job that carries it). Booking (step 14, install_scheduled): install_scheduling and install_agg_concurrent_jobs policy scope; HOA approval answered by the customer (none); the date 2026-10-19 lies within the 10-business-day reschedule offer window counted from 2026-10-07 (Columbus Day 10-12 skipped, window ends 2026-10-21). No time eligibility applies to these subjects (customer_notice governs reschedule rows only), so temporal_feasibility is [].

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target: install job IJ-2026-31846 (window contract RW-26-318402, factory order FO-2026-31377). Rows in aggregates: its four activity rows (a_r1, a_fee1, a_r2, a_r3); excluded: the closed 2021 door job IJ-2021-30472 (different job), the door contract's order and unit. The reschedule fee is correlated to a_r3 by its date 2026-10-06; the permit fee to the job's opened date; the capping to the booked crew date.

7. SEED. Customer profile (1949 home, ZIP 43214); 2021 door contract (closed), its order and job (closed) - history and near-misses; CareLine Plus plan SP-318455 active since 2021-07-06 (load-bearing parts discount); window contract (13 openings, senior, 15450.24 = 16094 x 0.96) with deposit 6180.10 (40 percent), final measure 2026-07-24 (3 oversize), oversize surcharge, exterior color and tempered change orders (one change order date, within the free count); door contract RD-26-307215 ordered (filing partner) and its order; window order delivered 2026-09-24 (job opened the same day, storage free to 2026-10-24, beyond the booked date); the job's reschedule history. Automatic clauses checked: no crew day has happened (no lead-safe fee or late-arrival credit owed yet), R2 had 88 h of notice (no company credit owed), customer reschedules 2 of max 3, no storage fee owed. Stale field: install_jobs.crew_days_planned 5 belongs to the released booking.

8. PERSONA. Ruth speaks warmly and plainly, volunteers only the capping wish and that she wants it on every window; ID details only when asked; her date (Monday, October 19), the HOA answer and her memory of the October 6 cancellation only when asked; she lets the agent book whatever has to be booked and accepts the stated price, runs the approval with the given details, and ends when the agent confirms. No prerequisite is named.

9. STANDARD SOLUTION AND RUN. Reads: find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, ZIP) -> find_install_jobs -> find_install_activities(job) -> find_window_contracts -> find_window_transactions -> find_door_contracts -> find_factory_orders -> find_service_plans. Writes: permit fee 89.40 (2026-09-24) and reschedule fee 37.50 (2026-10-06) in either order; booking 2026-10-19 / 6 crew days; customer capping approval 13 openings / 1342.59 / 2026-10-19. Commands run: check_task_tools (OK), replay_tasks --task 0 (det True, closure 19 = initial 19), check_compute --task 0 (COMPUTE OK, every factor_sensitivity and baseline_result recomputed equal), check_solvability --task 0 (OK), check_grounding --task 0 (OK), check_extended --task 0 (OK), check_cross_fire --task 0 (OK); order_t.py swapping steps 9-10 with 11-12: identical terminal state True. Revision log: (1) fee tools gained customer_id because the lead-safe gate binds customers.customer_id; (2) seed trimmed to the read closure (order milestones, warranty, service calls and 2021 job activities dropped; FK blanks set to null); (3) the old permit-fee near-miss was dropped with the 2021 job activities.

10. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the four rule texts alone: capping needs a booked date -> booking needs the permit fee (permitted job) and the release fee -> both fees are computable from the job, contracts and change orders; the same four writes and the same figures follow (89.40, 37.50, 6, 1342.59); no second reading of 'the most recent customer reschedule', 'latest completed measure' or 'released to the factory and not yet installed' fits the records.


12. REWORK ROUND 2 (render-source findings install_round1.md). R1: the capping overwrite no longer retires the general site-charge sentence; it retires the per-opening capping clause only (see 4). R2: base parameter_schema text, blueprint-known, no policy here reads it, no change. R3/R4/R5 concern task-1 policies (credit wait adder with no booked date, sill band, failed-access basis with no crew day held); their wording changed with the compute unchanged. Note: the permit filing fee's own_signed binding now belongs to the shared_filing_share factor (rewritten as an and/or read with the same values). No scored value changed: re-run check_compute OK with 89.40 / 37.50 / 6 / 1342.59 and every factor_sensitivity figure as before; full gate block re-run.

13. REWORK ROUND 3 (policy_kb S0-1/S0-2 and F0-2 source wording). Crew-date booking: the computation document now defines 'the units the crew plans for, which are the job's units' and 'the crew's daily pace, which is the method's openings per crew day'; the inspection hold-back ladder says its openings 'join the units the crew plans for'; the oversize ladder now reads only 'the units the crew plans for' and the oversize openings, naming no other factor (compute: new plumbing binding plan_units = unit_count + inspection_hold, read by plan_days). Capping: the computation document defines 'the priced openings, which are the openings on the contract the job installs'; the oversize ladder says each oversize opening 'counts as two / one and a half priced openings'; the volume ladder's bindings are now exactly what its tiers read (priced_openings, capping_price; the unweighted cap_openings binding was folded into priced_openings), so its document needs no 'as counted for capping' pointer. No scored value changed: check_compute OK with 89.40 / 37.50 / 6 / 1342.59 and the same factor_sensitivity figures.
user_scenario: You are Ruth Kowalski, seventy-one, a retired school librarian who lives in a 1949 brick-and-siding house in Columbus. You are polite, organized and a little chatty, and you like to understand what you are paying for, but you do not argue with prices once they are explained. You are calling Ridgeline about the thirteen new fiberglass windows you bought this summer; they are the dark bronze color you chose at the measure. Your reason for calling: you have decided you want the aluminum trim capping on the outside of all of your windows, so the old peeling white wood trim gets wrapped to match the new frames. The man who did the measure in July showed you what capping looks like and said you could add it before the crew comes, and you have finally made up your mind. You want it on every window, not just some, and you want it done as part of your installation. You are not asking for anything else. You do not know any prices, fees or how Ridgeline works out the charges, and you never guess at amounts. When the agent asks who you are, give your name; give your phone number, 6145550142, and your ZIP code, 43214, only when the agent asks for details to verify you. If asked for more, your email is ruth.kowalski53@gmail.com and your date of birth is February 17, 1955. You do not have your contract or job numbers handy and say so; the agent can look you up. If the agent asks about your earlier crew dates, you remember that you called on the evening of October 6 to cancel the crew that was coming on October 8, because your sister had surgery and you went to help her, and that earlier, at the end of September, you had moved your first date once as well; you do not bring this up yourself. If the agent says a crew date has to be booked, you would like the crew to come on Monday, October 19, because you are back home on the 17th; you accept whatever number of crew days the agent says the job needs. If the agent asks, there is no homeowners association and the house is not in a historic district, and you will have the rooms cleared and the blinds down before the crew arrives. If the agent explains that some charge has to be put on your job, or something has to be booked or recorded, before the capping can be added, you tell them to go ahead and do it, because you want everything done properly; you do not ask for any charge to be reduced or removed. When the agent tells you the price of the capping and gives you the approval to complete yourself, you accept the price and carry out the approval exactly with the details the agent gives you, then read back what it shows. Once you have completed the approval and the agent confirms the capping is on your job, you thank them warmly and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The permit administration fee and the late reschedule fee are parallel prerequisites of the crew-date booking. Neither computation reads what the other writes (the permit fee reads only the contracts and change orders; the reschedule fee counts reschedule rows and late_reschedule_fee rows, never permit_admin_fee rows), and their charge ids are derived from their own arguments, so the order between them is free. Run: replaying gold with the two write pairs swapped (actions 11-12 before 9-10) gives an identical terminal DB (order_t.py: identical terminal state: True), and both amounts (89.40 and 37.50) are unchanged. The booking must follow both (its prerequisite sentences), and the capping charge must follow the booking (its own prerequisite sentence).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the booking write the job has no scheduled_date: the capping computation cannot count a lead (it raises), the capping charge has no work date, and the terminal job row stays opened with crew_days_planned 5 instead of scheduled 2026-10-19 / 6.
Skipping the permit fee leaves permit_filings 0, the inspection hold-back 0 and the crew days booked 5 instead of 6; the terminal state also lacks the 89.40 permit_admin_fee row.

Skipping the late reschedule fee leaves the 2026-10-06 release without its fee, so the booking gate is not satisfied and the terminal state lacks the 37.50 late_reschedule_fee row dated 2026-10-06 (the crew days value itself is unchanged: this edge is a state gate).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario speaks only of adding aluminum capping to the outside trim of all her new windows and of when the crew will come; it never mentions a permit, a permit or filing fee, a late or reschedule fee, the released date as something owed, or booking as something to be sorted first. Her date preference (Monday, October 19) is given only when the agent says a crew date has to be booked, and her agreement to charges is a passive reaction to amounts the agent states.
